findings.text: The opening paragraphs tell a newcomer what Athena is, what a study is, and why this one exists: to show that every statement traces back to source lines. That quickly answers both "what is this" and "why does it matter".
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... A study is Athena's written reading of another software project

findings.text: "Start here" uses captain, yolo, green/red, and local-only landing before explaining any of them. Captain and yolo are only defined in the Glossary further down, and green/red are never defined anywhere, so a newcomer reading top to bottom hits terms they don't know.
findings.source: With the yolo setting off, the captain approves every PR merge and every local-only landing. With yolo on, firstmate merges green, in-scope work itself, and never a red one.

findings.text: "Home" is used here and in other places ("this home has no item", "a home's backlog") but has no Glossary entry. That makes it hard to understand what a secondmate is.
findings.source: A secondmate is a persistent home, not a backlog item.

findings.text: The study's internal id appears in the lede with no explanation. To a newcomer it is noise.
findings.source: This page is that study of firstmate, from firstmate-work-handling.

findings.text: The design-choice cards are titled only with opaque ids (ra1–ra6). A short descriptive title would let a reader skim for the choices they care about. The transition cards (t1–t11) at least show from-state → to-state.
findings.source: Heading "Why it is built this way": cards titled ra1 … ra6

findings.text: The Glossary is not in alphabetical order, so it is slow to look up a term met earlier on the page.
findings.source: Heading "Glossary": first entries are "code", "queued", "in-flight" … last entries "stale wake", "relaunch"

findings.text: The page ends with clear next actions for both projects and explains how to check a claim. This answers "what do I do next".
findings.source: Heading "Next steps": "Learn about Athena, and how to install and try it" / "Learn about firstmate ... and see how to use it"

findings.text: The page says plainly that nothing was run and every claim comes from reading the code. That honesty helps a newcomer judge how far to trust it.
findings.source: Heading "Limits of this study": "f1 could-not-run This study read the pinned tree only ... no failure or retry edge was observed"

findings.text: Several claims list the same source link twice, and c34 appears before c33. These are small flaws but they weaken the page's own message about careful tracing.
findings.source: Heading "Claims and sources": claim c2 lists docs/configuration.md:357-357 twice; c14 and c42 likewise repeat a source
